title: JD Vance's 'Mamaw' Set To Be Honored At Park. One Councilwoman Appears To Be Trying To Throw Wrench In Those Plans | The Daily Caller
text:
Vice President JD Vance’s grandmother is set to be honored at a park in Middletown, Ohio, however, one councilwoman appears to be throwing a wrench in the proposed plan.
Paul Horn, a Middletown councilman, proposed in December that a bench with a plaque memorializing Vance’s late grandmother, Bonnie Blanton Vance, be placed in Miami Park, near where she lived before passing away in 2005. In Vance’s best-selling memoir, “ Hillbilly Elegy ,” he wrote that his late grandmother, whom he called “Mamaw,” helped keep him on the straight-and-narrow path while growing up in the rust belt town. (RELATED: Forget Hillbilly Elegy. This Column Is The Best Thing JD Vance Has Ever Written)
“Maybe we think about a memorial or something strategically at Miami Park as a token of our appreciation of her choosing to live here … if you read the book and watched the movie, that person grounded him while his mother was trying to get clean and get her life together and was close to him,” Horn said at the December meeting, according to WCPO 9 News.
But on Tuesday, councilwoman Jennifer Carter pushed back on building a bench solely for Bonnie Vance during a discussion on the plan’s finalization and logistics.
“I think it would be nice if we put many grandmothers in the park. We have a lot of people in Middletown who have raised their children’s children,” she reportedly said. “I thought we were going to make Miami Park the grandmother’s park. I didn’t know it was for a specific family.”
Vice President JD Vance speaks during a conversation with conservative media personality Mercedes Schlapp at the annual Conservative Political Action Conference (CPAC) at the Gaylord National Resort & Convention Center at National Harbor in Oxon Hill, Maryland, on February 20, 2025. (Photo by Saul Loeb/AFP via Getty Images)
Horn responded that it may not be feasible to line the park with benches dedicated to other families and that the community ultimately “should feel good” that Vance grew up there, the outlet reported.
“The reason I brought it up is one: we should feel good that (Vance) came from our city,” Horn said. “And it is a memorial to help people understand when you are going through a difficult time, and you have to raise your children’s children, there is hope for the future.”
On the campaign trail in 2024, Vance spoke several times of his late grandmother, saying she was a “devout Christian” and a “tough old bird” who had apparently stashed away “19 loaded handguns” throughout her home. At a Republican National Convention, the then-vice presidential candidate described her as his “guardian angel.”
“I had a guardian angel by my side. She was an old woman who could barely walk, but she was tough as nails,” Vance said .
